implementation.activation: Candidate manifest is never active by default. Activation reopens pinned files/snapshots, checks unchanged contract/foundation, matched candidate/reference controller and observer coverage, actual GLM phase parameters and numeric case-limit records, public new-version pipeline interfaces, pinned reference commit/Node artifact, and independent reviews covering contract/snapshot/sampling/collector/grader/normalizer/controllers/blind/registration. Reviews bind exact manifest bytes and cannot name an implementation author as reviewer.
implementation.registration: A manifest-bound registry root exclusively reserves cohort/case/repetition before calling the reviewed observer. Fresh UUID run ID and nonce, reservation bytes, activation and manifest bindings are fsynced. Observer must inspect current executor/store/deployment/model/source facts and return the fresh challenge with a current timestamp, matching decrypted task and zero prior dispatches. Existing task/store/world receipt identities cannot become new trials. No legacy run/observation JSON import API exists.
implementation.dispatch: DispatchGate rechecks actual observer source bytes, all frozen files, registration and nonce bindings, current identity/model policy, original pending request ID, prior attempt count and native session identity. A hash-linked admission record with original request ID is fsynced before invoking the wrapped original callback. Distinct subsequent model/tool IDs work; duplicate IDs, drift, missing original requests, extra unobserved attempts and changed history fail closed.
implementation.receipt_meaning: Admission records prove gate ordering only, not successful transport, supplier usage, mutation, business completion or formal acceptance. A callback failure/crash consumes its original request ID; original transport and business receipts remain necessary. Unknown usage/cost is not filled with zero.
implementation.reference: Reference observation requires the exact pinned commit, clean working tree, actual Node byte hash, native session identifier/store hash and an original RPC audit observer. The gate does not fabricate SQLite/RPC evidence and cannot make current incomplete reference controllers ready.
implementation.blind_boundary: Only an independently reviewed public blind-interface descriptor/implementation is hash-bound. No heldout case enumeration or loading is implemented; known heldout directories and build_cases.py are rejected before reads, including hashing.

trust_boundary: Trusted local collectors and independent reviewers establish factual authenticity and completeness. The registry verifies bindings, current callback ordering and file consistency; it is not cryptographic remote attestation or protection against a malicious operator rewriting the entire registry and all artifacts.

Review identities are trusted local review artifacts, not cryptographic signatures. A reviewer must inspect actual implementations and completeness before supplying a passed review; a self-consistent fabricated review cannot become true by hashing it.

A clean_world_sha256 value must identify the fresh nonce-bound initial-world observation receipt, not just identical business fixture content. Source snapshots must enumerate the complete executed dependency/code set; completeness requires independent review.
The actual repository manifest intentionally has no authors, covered cases, registry root or pipeline artifacts. No release is activated and L1-L3 are not declared complete.
